stories.title: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization
stories.summary: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll to advise on responsible AI for national security modernization, cyber resilience, and collaboration with U.S. allies.

sources.name: OpenAI
sources.title: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: OpenAI hires former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for national security role
sources.text: OpenAI has hired former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as senior counselor for national security modernization, a newly created role at the company . Driscoll will focus on how artificial intelligence can be used to strengthen U.S. national security and cybersecurity, OpenAI said, while his updated LinkedIn profile also lists his new position. He will work with OpenAI's senior leadership and external partners, with a particular focus on helping U.S. allies adopt advanced AI responsibly. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the U.S. has "an extraordinary opportunity to work with other countries to spread the adoption of democratic AI," and that Driscoll's appointment would help strengthen American leadership in the technology. "National security requirements are changing faster than at any time in the past fifty years," Driscoll said. He added that AI could help reduce paperwork, process information and deliver answers more quickly to those working in national security. The appointment comes after Driscoll stepped down as Army secretary earlier this year after months of reported tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. An Iraq war veteran, Driscoll pushed efforts to modernize the U.S. military, including expanding access to drone and counter-drone technologies among U.S. allies, according to a previous U.S. Army announcement. Driscoll also met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv in November 2025 to discuss a U.S.-proposed peace plan aimed at ending the war with Russia, according to a statement from the Presidential Office of Ukraine. At OpenAI, Driscoll will work with government officials, industry leaders, academic institutions and allied organizations to advance what the company calls "democratic AI." He will also help internal teams understand the operational needs of national security institutions, building on OpenAI's efforts to strengthen cyber resilience and protect essential services through its Daybreak program .

stories.title: OpenAI vai ‘aposentar’ ChatGPT Classic no começo de 2027; veja o que muda
stories.summary: O app do ChatGPT para desktop testará a integração entre os modos chat e Work.

sources.name: Tecmundo
sources.title: OpenAI vai ‘aposentar’ ChatGPT Classic no começo de 2027; veja o que muda
sources.text: OpenAI encerra conta e alerta Polícia Federal sobre homem que planejou atentado contra Lula no ChatG Entenda a ação da OpenAI ao banir a conta de um usuário e acionar a Polícia Federal e o TSE após detectar planos de ataque contra o presidente Lula no ChatGPT. A OpenAI vai aposentar o ChatGPT Classic em 30 de janeiro de 2027. A data foi divulgada para usuários do antigo aplicativo. Ao mesmo tempo, a empresa prepara uma experiência unificada para o chatbot e o agente ChatGPT Work no programa mais recente. O ChatGPT Classic ganhou esse nome após a estreia da versão repaginada do aplicativo desktop em julho deste ano , que reunia o chat, o ChatGPT Work e o Codex em uma única interface. Na época, a OpenAI buscava ampliar o acesso às ferramentas de inteligência artificial agênticas. O ChatGPT Classic, por sua vez, continuou oferecendo uma experiência semelhante à do ChatGPT disponível na web, com histórico de conversas, biblioteca, projetos e outros recursos de texto. Com o passar dos meses, o aplicativo ficou defasado em relação à nova versão, que recebia funcionalidades inéditas , como a capacidade de selecionar o nível de esforço de raciocínio. “Este aplicativo será desativado em 30 de janeiro de 2027. Acesse os recursos mais recentes no novo aplicativo do ChatGPT. Todo o seu histórico de conversas será transferido para que você possa continuar de onde parou”, diz o aviso encaminhado aos usuários. Dentro do novo app ChatGPT Desktop, a OpenAI prepara uma experiência de uso que reúne o chatbot e o Work em um só ambiente . A mudança torna a linha entre as conversas puramente por texto e as funções agênticas mais tênue, poupando o usuário de escolher entre um modo ou outro. A integração entre agentes e chatbots segue uma tendência de mercado entre as gigantes provedoras de IA . Pouco a pouco, Google e Anthropic também aproximaram as experiências de chat e agente de IA, às vezes reduzindo a escolha a um simples interruptor na tela. A grande diferença entre um chatbot convencional e um agente como o ChatGPT Work é a autonomia para a execução de tarefas. Enquanto o chat é voltado principalmente à interação com o usuário, o Work pode assumir tarefas mais complexas, utilizar ferramentas e executar diferentes etapas sob orientação humana. O teste começará com um pequeno grupo de pessoas , segundo um e-mail enviado pela OpenAI. “A mudança permitirá que você leve a exploração de uma ideia para a execução no ChatGPT, tudo em um só lugar. Você pode trazer seus arquivos e plugins e pedir o ChatGPT para construir um site, criar uma apresentação, ou fazer coisas por você na web, enquanto revisa e orienta seu trabalho. O Codex continuará uma experiência distinta dentro do app ChatGPT Desktop”. Junto com a transição, a OpenAI também planeja implementar uma franquia de uso compartilhada entre o ChatGPT e o Codex , substituindo os limites separados. A novidade está prevista para dezembro de 2026 nos planos Plus, Pro e Business. Segundo a companhia, a mudança não deve fazer com que a maioria dos usuários precise esperar pela renovação dos limites com mais frequência. O consumo será calculado conforme o modelo utilizado e a complexidade da tarefa. As conversas ilimitadas no modo “Instant” continuarão incluídas nos planos contemplados e não consumirão a franquia compartilhada. Quer ficar por dentro das novidades do mundo da tecnologia? sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: OpenAI vai unificar limites do ChatGPT e Codex; veja o que muda
sources.text: A OpenAI vai unificar os limites de uso do ChatGPT e do Codex a partir de dezembro, mas a empresa ainda não divulgou o dia exato em que a alteração entrará em vigor. A mudança afetará os assinantes dos planos Plus, Pro e Business. Segundo a OpenAI, a novidade acompanha a integração dos recursos de inteligência artificial agêntica do Work à experiência principal do ChatGPT. Com o novo modelo, o consumo será calculado em tokens , unidades de informação processadas pelos modelos de IA. O gasto dependerá do modelo escolhido e da complexidade de cada tarefa. Assim, solicitações mais exigentes vão consumir uma parcela maior da cota. A mudança também terá impacto no uso combinado das duas ferramentas. Uma longa sessão de programação no Codex, por exemplo, reduzirá o limite disponível para tarefas complexas no ChatGPT. O mesmo vale no sentido contrário. A exceção fica por conta das conversas no Instant chat , que não descontarão tokens da cota compartilhada. Até então, ChatGPT, Work e Codex tinham limites independentes , com cotas próprias para envio de arquivos, geração de imagens e interações por voz. Os assinantes do Plus também contavam com uma janela de uso de cinco horas para o Codex e o Work e uma cota semanal. A nova estrutura vai concentrar o consumo dos serviços em um único limite. Quando a cota acabar, os usuários terão três alternativas : aguardar a renovação do limite, fazer upgrade do plano ou comprar créditos adicionais para continuar usando os recursos. A OpenAI também vai mostrar o saldo restante e o tempo estimado até a próxima renovação no menu “Configurações” > “Uso”. A OpenAI afirma que está preparando a transição para evitar interrupções nos fluxos de trabalho. A expectativa é que a maioria dos usuários mantenha uma frequência de renovação de limites semelhante à atual. A estratégia também acompanha uma mudança adotada pela Anthropic , que unificou as cotas do Claude para o chat, o Cowork e o Claude Code . A documentação da OpenAI ainda não informa qual será o volume de tokens disponível em cada plano . Também faltam detalhes sobre a frequência de renovação dos limites e possíveis mudanças nas regras de uso. Outro ponto em aberto é o impacto da novidade nas assinaturas Free e Go . Até o momento, a empresa não confirmou se esses planos também terão alterações na contabilização do consumo. Se você gostou do texto, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ ChatGPT Codex e Claude Code: o que muda entre as IAs para programação? ”.

stories.summary: Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times. The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on Tuesday, saying that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search "will be entirely off" for K-12 student accounts […]

sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.title: Google is entirely disabling Search in schools that don’t want AI
sources.text: Students in schools that reject Google’s AI will see notices that Search isn’t available. Students in schools that reject Google’s AI will see notices that Search isn’t available. Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times . The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on Tuesday, saying that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search “will be entirely off” for K-12 student accounts unless “administrators explicitly turn them on.” Administrators will not be given the option to toggle Gemini-powered features off without disabling Search, however. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the NYT , “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” adding that schools that disable Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” Google didn’t immediately respond to The Verge ’s request for comment. The announcement comes just months after Google turned its Gemini AI assistant on by default inside the Google Classroom app, which is used by more than 150 million teachers and students globally. The move added to skepticism surrounding Google’s introduction of AI in schools amid reports of declining test scores and other impacts on students’ learning abilities . Last month, lawmakers pressed Google on the “potential harms” of putting its AI products in schools. Although Google is no longer turning on AI features in schools by default, this choice comes at a cost. Several lawmakers and local leaders have responded to Google’s move to block Search, with Sen. Bernie Sanders (D-VT) calling it “extortion” and NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani saying , “no corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children.” Rohit Chopra, California’s Secretary of Business & Consumer Services, wrote that Big Tech shouldn’t be able to “strong-arm schools.” Google argues that this change will “give schools more choice, not less,” adding that schools can choose to turn off each service on or off individually. The company is also attempting to address concerns about students using its AI features to find “shortcuts” instead of solving problems themselves. Google is embedding its Guided Learning feature, which is supposed to help students work through problems , into its AI Overviews in Search. Google will begin testing this feature in select US schools this month. Update, November 3rd: Added responses from lawmakers and Google.

sources.name: SiliconANGLE
sources.title: Google offers tepid response to accusations it would hold Search hostage if schools restrict AI tools
sources.text: Google LLC today faced a barrage of criticism after the company warned that if schools restricted their students from using its artificial intelligence tools, the same students wouldn’t be able to use Search. The fallout came after the company announced a slew of new products for classrooms. Teachers and schools were told that the new AI tools would come with features that will allow for limitations or complete blocks of the features, but if teachers or schools should take that route, students would not be able to use Google Search. Some media described it as rather cunning behavior from the tech giant. “After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search,” Google said in a blog post . “Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.” A New York Times article followed the announcement and explained that where schools have banned the use of AI or if they limit AI in the classroom, the students would not have access to Search. Since Google’s suite of products are a mainstay in classrooms all over the U.S., the backlash was imminent. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote on X. “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech.” Sen. Bernie Sanders from Vermont was equally chastising, writing on X, “Google is threatening schools” and using what amounts to “extortion.” Lina Khan, former chair of the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, was similarly unimpressed, writing that Google was trying to, “coerce schools into adopting AI.” Google was quick to respond. In a post on X, the company said its new policy is about giving schools more control over how students use AI. Gemini chatbot, Gemini Notebook, the company explained, will be turned off by default, but “schools are in control.” “We are also updating Search for schools to make it better for learning,” Google added. “Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.” The company explained that it was aware of the dangers of students embracing the “AI shortcut” and effectively not engaging their brains. However, Google seemed to ignore the basis of the criticism regarding Search not being available when AI functions were turned off. Given the company has found itself under the gun many times in recent years for its business tactics, and in light of studies showing overuse of technology can have a harmful impact on children, the response seemed to critics tepid at best. stories.title: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
stories.summary: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
sources.text: Fal , a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported . The startup announced its Series E and F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.) The latest round (Series F) comes amid soaring demand for inference services, the process of running an AI model that’s already been trained to generate outputs, particularly from customers relying on open source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted. Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations . But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials. Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon. sources.name: SiliconANGLE
sources.title: Generative media inference startup fal raises $1.3B at a $16B valuation
sources.text: Generative media inference startup fal today announced it has raised $1.3 billion in new funding at a valuation of $16 billion, according to Bloomberg. The company will spend the money on computing power and on hiring beyond its current 185 employees. Fal provides a cloud platform for running image, video and audio generation models, and developers reach all of them through a single application programming interface. Entertainment studios, advertising agencies and game developers are among the customers using those models in production, according to the company. In-house researchers also post-train some of those models to run faster. Over the past year that work has centered on video, in partnership with the open- and closed-source developers that build the models. Some of the deals pay fal licensing fees or a share of revenue, Bloomberg reported. Co-founder and Chief Executive Burkay Gur told the outlet the round is as large as it is because demand has surged and serving it takes more compute. “We hit a point in summer where we were not able to serve our customers and had to rate-limit them,” he said. Pretraining a model of fal’s own is not on the near-term agenda, said Gur, who did not rule it out for later. Annualized revenue at fal passed $800 million earlier this year, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. The valuation puts fal just behind rival inference provider Fireworks AI Inc., which closed $1.5 billion in funding at a $17.5 billion valuation in July . Several people familiar with the finances of inference companies told TechCrunch that gross margins across the sector remain thin because compute is expensive to buy or lease. Gur started the company in 2021 with Chief Technology Officer Gorkem Yurtseven. His resume includes leading machine learning work at Coinbase Global Inc. and an engineering role at Oracle Corp. Yurtseven was previously a developer at Amazon.com Inc. Bessemer Venture Partners led the Series F round, and its partner Talia Goldberg is joining the board of Features & Labels Inc., as fal is formally known. Nvidia Corp., Sound Ventures, HOF Capital and T. Rowe Price Group Inc. also participated. Fal described Nvidia as a strategic investor. Today’s announcement also covered an April round led by Sequoia Capital. That Series E round raised $350 million at an $8 billion valuation, per Bloomberg, and fal said the two rounds come to $1.65 billion combined. Last December , the company raised $140 million at a $4.5 billion valuation. Investors have now put more than $1.9 billion into the company. sources.name: The Guardian Technology
sources.title: Google says there’s no way to use Search without using artificial intelligence
sources.text: In announcement geared to schools, tech giant shows how entwined AI is with the world’s most popular website Google just acknowledged that you can’t use Google Search without using artificial intelligence . The search giant announced a slate of new AI products for classrooms and schools on Tuesday as well as more ways for teachers and schools to limit or restrict use of those AI tools. The company said the schools should have control over whether students use AI in the classroom. There’s one catch, though: if a school or teacher blocks the use of Google’s AI features, students won’t be able to use Google Search. “After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search,” company executives wrote in a blogpost. “Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.” In a comment to the New York Times , Chris Phillips, Google’s vice-president for education, said that there is no Google Search without AI. “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” said Phillips. A school-wide ban on AI would mean that students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available”, he told the Times. The Guardian also reached out to Google but did not hear back by publication. To some, the move reads like a penalty for not implementing Google’s AI features. New York City’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani, who recently imposed a one-year moratorium on generative AI tools in city schools through the eighth grade, said Google was exploiting its near-total control of online search. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Mamdani posted on X. “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech.” Lina Khan, former chair of the US Federal Trade Commission, echoed his statement, tweeting that Google was using its monopoly on search to “to coerce schools into adopting AI”. The ubiquity of Google Search has long made it a critical tool for students, and losing access to it may prove enough of a reason to opt in to using new AI features for schools. Google has also maintained a stranglehold on technology in US classrooms for years by offering cheap and free products. From Gmail and Google Docs to Google Classroom and Google Chromebooks, the company’s suite of software and hardware solutions are among the most widely used in schools. One of the new features Google announced today was Guided Learning, an AI study tool that “coaches students through the process of problem solving” rather than giving them the answer. The company is planning to integrate Guided Learning directly into Google Search. “For example, if a student pastes a complex physics problem or asks for help writing a book report in Search, they’ll see prompts to help them think critically and work through the concepts, without going directly to the answer,” the company wrote in a blogpost. Lila Byock, founder of Schools Beyond Screens, called Google’s announcement a “hostile ultimatum”. Schools Beyond Screens is a national coalition of parents and teachers advocating for more student-centered policies on the use of screens in schools. “This kind of bullying has no place in our schools,” Byock said in a statement. “Educational value – not shareholder value – must determine which products are used by students and regulators must intervene to prevent big tech from exploiting schoolchildren for profit.”

sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
sources.text: ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI. ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI. In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how-to explanation. (Fry did not specify the source of the Google search volume number.) Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade. During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree. (OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in-house search index, although there is still some speculation that it routes some queries through Google.) The news comes amid an ongoing search engine shake-up, as Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third-party sites and invests heavily in AI tools — not just AI Overview but also additional generative AI capabilities , including personalized search results with visualizations and charts. But as search queries increasingly route through OpenAI and other AI labs’ services, other companies are investing in the same types of AI-focused search experience, even if they call it something else: for OpenAI, it’s “Intelligent UI,” or creating a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response. “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” Fry said. Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year. OpenAI has defended its ads in the past, and Fry told reporters they hadn’t produced a lasting backlash. “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” he said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.” OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before. “Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: ChatGPT já alcança 20% do volume de buscas do Google, diz OpenAI
sources.text: O ChatGPT está ampliando sua participação no mercado de buscas na internet. Segundo a OpenAI , o chatbot já processa um volume de consultas equivalente a um quinto do registrado pelo Google . A declaração indica o avanço da ferramenta como alternativa aos mecanismos tradicionais de pesquisa, embora a distância entre as duas plataformas ainda seja significativa. O número foi apresentado por Adam Fry, responsável pelo produto de consumo do ChatGPT, durante evento da OpenAI realizado na segunda-feira (2). Segundo ele, a companhia considera uma busca toda consulta enviada pelo usuário que resulta em uma pesquisa na web. Perguntas simples, como pedidos para definir um termo ou explicar como fazer alguma coisa, não entram nessa conta. A empresa, porém, não informou a origem do número utilizado para comparar o volume de pesquisas do ChatGPT com o do Google. A disputa não envolve apenas responder a perguntas. A OpenAI também está desenvolvendo experiências de pesquisa mais visuais e interativas dentro do ChatGPT. A companhia chama essa abordagem de “Intelligent UI” (interface inteligente, em tradução livre). A proposta é transformar as respostas do chatbot em ambientes interativos, com elementos visuais e recursos que permitam ao usuário explorar informações sem sair da conversa. “É para lá que o futuro dessa tecnologia está indo. Você está conversando com uma tela”, afirmou Fry. Outro ponto estratégico é a publicidade. Assim como o Google, a OpenAI enxerga nos anúncios uma possível fonte de receita para seus serviços, especialmente diante da possibilidade de uma abertura de capital no início de 2027. Fry afirmou que a publicidade não provocou reação negativa duradoura entre os usuários e que a maioria das pessoas parece não se incomodar com os anúncios no produto. A empresa anunciou no mês anterior que começaria a exibir imagens de produtos e serviços patrocinados no ChatGPT. Até então, os anúncios apresentavam principalmente o nome da companhia, seu logotipo e um link para o produto. “Os anúncios talvez tenham nos mostrado que poderíamos estar fazendo isso ainda mais”, declarou o executivo. Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.
